summary.text: 考 is traditionally analyzed as 老 with its lower 匕 omitted, combined with 丂 as a sound marker. The account is plausible rather than settled: a competing proposal treats 丂 as an original graph reused for ‘father’, with 老 added as a meaning marker. The character is attested for ‘father’ and separately for ‘consider/estimate’; the evidence does not establish that one meaning developed from the other. [ref020, ref022, ref025]

formation.text: Phonosemantic under the favored analysis: the reduced 老 contributes the category ‘old/elder’, and 丂 marks sound. A competing semantic analysis treats 老 as a classifier added to 丂 when the latter was reused for ‘father’. The dossier does not settle between these accounts. [ref020, ref025]

components.text: 老 appears in a reduced form, written 耂 here; the favored account says its lower 匕 is usually omitted. It contributes the ‘old/elder’ category in this analysis, though the role of 老 is disputed by the alternative account. [ref020, ref025]

丂 is the sound element in the favored analysis. Its own proposed origins conflict: it has been interpreted as a branch, cane/staff, or axe handle, but its referent and original name are not established. [ref020, ref023, ref026]

sound_limitation.text: The dossier gives a shared Middle Chinese transcription, khawX, and modern Mandarin kǎo for 丂 and 考, but local Old Chinese forms differ and were not externally verified here. These comparisons do not establish the component’s historical sound role independently. [ref030, ref035]

sound.text: 丂 and 考 are both recorded as Middle Chinese khawX and modern Mandarin kǎo. Local Baxter–Sagart data give distinct Old Chinese forms, so the shared later readings alone cannot establish the proposed ancient sound relation. [ref030, ref035]

history.text: The received graph is traditionally explained as 老省 with 丂 supplying sound. The favored inscriptional account says early Western Zhou writing used 老 for both ‘old’ and ‘father’, then added 丂 to distinguish 考, commonly omitting 老’s lower 匕. An alternative reverses the explanatory emphasis: 丂 was reused for ‘father’ and 老 added as a semantic classifier. The dossier reports this disagreement without settling the graph’s origin. [ref020, ref021, ref025]

The cited source reports bronze examples of 考 for ‘father’ and ‘consider/estimate’, and phonetic uses for 孝 and 巧. These examples are reported rather than independently inspected here, and their dates are not supplied. [ref022, ref025, ref033]
攷 is listed as a variant of 考, but the dossier does not establish when the forms overlapped or provide a fuller graphic chronology for their relationship. [ref024, ref027]

uncertainties.text: The original referent and name of 丂 remain disputed. Because its original pronunciation is not established, the proposal that it was borrowed to write ‘father’ cannot be confirmed by an object-name sound match. [ref023, ref026]
The cited examples do not date the earliest uses of ‘father’ or ‘consider/estimate’, nor show that the latter developed semantically from the former. [ref022, ref025]

The shared Middle Chinese and Mandarin readings of 丂 and 考 do not erase their distinct, locally reported Old Chinese reconstructions; those reconstructions were not independently verified against the inspected external table. [ref030, ref035]

senses.text: The traditional lexicographic explanation glosses 考 as ‘old’; whether this reflects the graph’s earliest meaning is not independently established. [ref003, ref021]
The dossier reports bronze uses of 考 for ‘father’; the cited account says this often refers to a deceased father, though not invariably. [ref022, ref025]
A reported bronze example uses 考 for ‘consider/estimate’. It does not establish when this sense arose or a semantic path from ‘father’. [ref022, ref025]
The supplied definitions give the common current sense as ‘examine, test; investigate’. The dossier does not establish its chronology relative to the older reported uses. [ref006, ref014]

limitations.text: The evidence gives historical glosses and reported examples but does not establish a chronology or semantic transitions among ‘old’, ‘father’, ‘consider/estimate’, and current ‘examine/test’. [ref022, ref025]

overview.text: 考 is analyzed as a reduced form of 老 joined to 丂 as a sound marker. It is used for ‘father’ and for ‘consider/examine’, but the evidence does not show that one meaning grew out of the other. [ref020, ref022, ref025]

components.text: 耂 is the reduced 老 element in the favored analysis; it supplies the ‘old/elder’ category, though another account gives it a classifier role. [ref020, ref025]
丂 is proposed as the sound element, but its ancient referent and name are disputed, limiting what the sound comparison can prove. [ref023, ref026, ref030, ref035]

relationships.text: In the favored analysis, 耂 is reduced 老 and contributes the ‘old/elder’ category; the competing analysis treats 老 as a classifier added to 丂. [ref020, ref025]

The traditional and favored inscriptional accounts assign 丂 the sound role. Shared Middle Chinese and Mandarin readings are reported, but distinct local Old Chinese forms and unresolved identity limit the independent force of this comparison. [ref020, ref021, ref030, ref035]
The official character dictionary lists 攷 among the variant forms of 考; the timing and fuller history of their overlap are not established here. [ref024, ref027]
